name: Firozpur–Shipki La Highway

timeline.event: Work begins on the historic Hindustan–Tibet Road during Lord Dalhousie's time
The corridor gets its current number, NH 5, in the national highway renumbering

history: NH 5 runs from Firozpur near the Pakistan border across the Punjab plains through Ludhiana, then climbs past Kalka and Solan to Shimla. From there it follows the deep valley of the Sutlej river through Kinnaur all the way to Shipki La, the mountain pass where the Sutlej enters India from Tibet. The hill section follows the famous Hindustan–Tibet Road, which the British began building in the 1850s.
facts: The hill section follows the historic Hindustan–Tibet Road, begun in the 1850s.
From Rampur onwards the road runs through the gorge of the Sutlej river in Kinnaur.
Some Kinnaur stretches are carved straight into cliff faces high above the river.
Shipki La, the highway's end point, is the pass where the Sutlej river flows into India from Tibet.
The final stretch beyond Khab towards Shipki La lies in a restricted border zone.

sources.title: NHAI — National Highways Authority of India
